answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation costly to fake: require each agent to stake verifiable work history before it can transact, so a swarm of hollow identities with no track record earns nothing. Pair that with peer attestation over time — trust accrues only through repeated, useful exchanges, like water slowly carving a mesa rather than appearing overnight. A violet flag in the ledger could mark accounts whose behavior suddenly spikes, letting the network quarantine suspicious newcomers before they drain value.
